Class CausalFrontier

java.lang.Object
io.parsley.CausalFrontier
public final class CausalFrontier extends Object
The engine/consumer horizon: the highest offset the causal processor has admitted on each topic-partition, keyed by the topic's Kafka UUID so that topic deletion and recreation produce a different identity even when the name is reused.

Instances are immutable. observe(CausalPosition) and merge(CausalFrontier) return new frontiers.

For paths without a real AdminClient UUID, derive one via CausalPosition.deriveUuid(String) and call observe(CausalPosition) directly.

Converting to dependencies

Call toDependencies() to turn the frontier into a CausalDependencies that can be stamped onto a produced record or handed to another service. This is intentionally explicit — it makes the "I depend on everything I have seen" trade-off visible at the call site. For a single consumed record's causal context, prefer CausalDependencies.fromRecord(ConsumerRecord) instead.

    • toDependencies

      public CausalDependencies toDependencies()
      Converts this frontier to a CausalDependencies that asserts "I require at least everything I have seen." Use this to propagate the full consumer horizon as a causal token; prefer CausalDependencies.fromRecord(ConsumerRecord) when only one record's context matters.
      Returns:
      a CausalDependencies equivalent to this frontier

    • positions

      public List<CausalPosition> positions()
      Returns the current positions as an unordered list of CausalPositions.
      Returns:
      the positions; never null

    • toBytes

      public byte[] toBytes()
      Serialises this frontier to a compact binary form compatible with CausalDependencies.toBytes().

      Wire format

      [byte  version=0x01]
[int   count]
for each entry:
  [long  topicId.mostSignificantBits]
  [long  topicId.leastSignificantBits]
  [int   partition]
  [long  offset]
      Returns:
      the serialised frontier

      Returns:

      Throws:
